_about: Brand tokens shared by the web game and the iOS app. Colours are #RRGGBB. Line weights are multiples of the board scale (points per triangle side), except the 1px hairline. fontScale (default 1) enlarges every text size for fonts with a small x-height.

logo._about: HEXGEN built from the game's own triangles, on the board's sideways lattice (triangles point left and right, as in the bin), at half a board triangle per cell. Each glyph is rows of '#' (filled) and '.' (empty), one character per column; a cell points right when row + column is even. Strokes run along the lattice's 30° diagonals, after the Merkur typeface by Malwin Béla Hürkey; glyphs are four columns by nine rows. Glyphs sit gap columns apart and lines lineGap rows apart, kept even so every glyph keeps its triangles' directions.

daily._about: The app's Daily Dial: a three-minute sprint, the same for everyone each UTC day, with one or two modifiers found nowhere else. The menu button shows the day's modifiers (joined by and), the day's best, and the streak. In play the modifiers sit under the timer. A paused daily hides its board and counts back in. %d and %@ fill in.

walkthrough._about: The app's first launch goes into a one-minute learning round (label), opening on a start card (introTitle, introBody, start, skip). The bot plays its first seconds, then hands over. Its captions stay short (about 32 characters, one idea each, never a 'don't') and follow what's on screen, in order: pile under a slowed close-up of a triangle landing; hex under the bot's first hex, in a mid-game bin with every colour; turn as it pulls back (on touch, drag and spin instead, as a ghost finger acts out each move; other inputs get the controls line under turn). After the glow, the bin fills most of the way (filling) and the player keeps it from overflowing (makeRoom); if it overflows, over. After the player's first hex, swap names the bot's glow demo, or swap or drain names a glow the player fired. done, doneBody, and recommend close the round, which offers every mode with a sprint first.

howTo._about: The app's rules page, in tabs by what a player came for: basics to start playing (with the lesson), scoring to do better, modes to choose a game (each mode's menu symbol beside it, then the daily's modifiers), and controls (one rule per input, the one in hand first). Each rule names its section and its drawing (art: a HowToArt drawing, a mode or menu symbol, or an input's symbol). only limits a rule to ios or tvos; input names the InputKind a controls rule is for. keys is a rule's table: an action, then what does it, per column (columns names them; one column needs no name). A key that starts sf: is an SF Symbol, with its spoken name after |. {confirm}, {cancel}, {sides} fill in for the input in hand. lead is a tab's one line under its name.

rules.title: the bin.
rules.body: triangles fall into the bin. when there's no room for the next one, the game is over.

rules.title: the dial.
rules.body: the dial covers six triangles. turn it to spin them around its centre. gravity stops under the dial, so it can hold pieces in place.

rules.title: hexes.
rules.body: six triangles of one colour around a point make a hex, and it clears, wherever it is in the bin.

rules.title: points.
rules.body: every hex scores 100 × your level. clear several at once and each one counts.

rules.title: levels.
rules.body: your level is the number of colours in play. every 6 hexes adds one, up to 8, and triangles arrive faster, so each new colour makes every hex worth 100 more.

rules.title: speed.
rules.body: SLOW scores half points and FAST one and a half times. choose it in SETUP. the daily and versus always play at normal speed.

rules.title: glowing pieces.
rules.body: clear a glowing triangle in a hex to fire its power. drain empties the bottom two rows; swap turns one colour into another.

rules.title: SPECTRUM.
rules.body: start with 3 colours and gain one every 4 hexes. clear 48 hexes, in any colours, to win.

rules.title: ENDLESS.
rules.body: start with 2 colours and play until the bin fills.

rules.title: SPRINT.
rules.body: score as much as you can in 3 minutes.

rules.title: DAILY.
rules.body: a sprint that's the same for everyone today, with one of these rule changes, or a help and a twist together.

rules.title: VERSUS.
rules.body: 2 to 4 players, a bin each, the same triangles for everyone. SPRINT RACE is the best score in 3 minutes, SURVIVAL the last bin standing, FIRST TO WIN the first to finish SPECTRUM.

rules.title: CO-OP.
rules.body: two players, one bin, one score, a dial each. the dials can't overlap. play it with a Game Center friend from ONLINE, or as CO-OP in the VERSUS lobby on Apple TV.

rules.title: big board.
rules.body: a SETUP choice for playing alone: bigger triangles and 6 colours, so SPECTRUM is won at 36 hexes. it keeps its own best scores.

rules.title: touch.
rules.body: the wheel beside the bin spins either way, and so does a two-finger twist on the board.

rules.title: controller.
rules.body: Xbox, PlayStation and other controllers. the left stick moves like the d-pad. paused, A or cross plays on and B or circle goes to the menu.

rules.title: remote.
rules.body: paused, click plays on and back goes to the menu.

rules.title: phone.
rules.body: open Hexgen on an iPhone, choose CONNECT and enter the code on the menu. the phone becomes a controller.

rules.title: keyboard.
rules.body: paused, space or return plays on and esc goes to the menu.

rules.title: playing together.
rules.body: in VERSUS, every controller, remote, keyboard and phone is a player of its own, with its own controls. {confirm} joins, {sides} picks the game, {confirm} again starts, and {cancel} leaves.

unlocks._about: Every MAIN win and every lifetime-hexes milestone unlocks the next skin, in list order.

effects._about: One colour at a time: ink is the current strobe hue and the pieces are tints of it (positive mixes toward white, negative toward black). Every hex clear hard-cuts to the next hue, with a one-frame flash, at most three a second.
